topics: 🧑‍⚖️ When Is a Witness Disqualified Mid-Way? — the 'beginning and end' principle, and what 'and he is a witness' really excludes
💰 Still Counted as 'Poor' — a dying father's fortune, and a leased-out ship
⚖️ New Mishna: Age and Sex Follow the Person Valuated, Locked In at the Moment of the Vow
📅 Where Exactly Do the Age Brackets Switch Over? — a gezeira shava, and Rabbi Eliezer's stricter reading
🗓️ 'A Year' Across the Torah — Calendar Year, or Exact Anniversary?

overview.title: 📖 Overview: Fixing Every Boundary Precisely
overview.subtitle: Arakhin 18a–18b
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The daf closes the discussion of a witness's fitness with the principle that one who was fit both when he saw the event and when he testifies remains valid even if temporarily disqualified in between. It then finishes clarifying why a leper is still considered 'poor' even with a fortune technically coming his way: his dying father hasn't yet died, and his cargo ship is leased to others whose rent isn't yet due. A new mishna states that a valuation's age- and sex-based sum follows the person being valuated rather than the vower, fixed permanently at the moment the vow is spoken — paralleled to how a pearl is assessed by its immediate local market. The next mishna maps out exactly how the Torah's three age brackets transition, learned via a verbal analogy, with Rabbi Eliezer requiring a full extra month past each threshold rather than a single day. The daf closes with a baraita cataloguing several other Torah time periods, each calculated as an exact anniversary rather than the calendar year.

slides.title: 🧑‍⚖️ When Is a Witness Disqualified Mid-Way?
slides.subtitle: A 'beginning and end' principle, applied to testimony

nodes.content: ❓ A witness became temporarily unfit (deaf, blind, incompetent, or too closely related) between seeing an event and testifying about it, but was fit at both the START and the END — is his testimony valid?
✅ Yes: 'anyone whose beginning and end are in a state of fitness is fit,' even if disqualified in the interim

columns.label: Why different from valuation vows?
columns.content: Testimony depends only on valid SEEING and valid TELLING (Leviticus 5:1) — both occurred, regardless of the interim

columns.label: So what does 'and he is a witness' exclude?
columns.content: Not interim fitness — rather, that the witness must be explicitly SINGLED OUT by name, not merely one of an anonymous crowd addressed collectively

slides.title: 💰 Still Counted as 'Poor' — Two Edge Cases
slides.subtitle: A leper's offering tracks only what he actually possesses right now
rows: His father is moribund (gosess) and will leave him a fortune, but hasn't died yet
He does not legally own the inheritance until his father actually dies
His ship is at sea loaded with valuable cargo, but the ship itself is leased to others
The cargo belongs to the lessee, and rent isn't owed until the lease ends

callout.label: Underlying view:
callout.text: This follows Rabbi Eliezer's broader position that business assets used for one's livelihood — a plow-team, a rental donkey — aren't seized to satisfy Temple debts.

slides.title: ⚖️ New Mishna: Age and Sex Follow the Person Valuated
slides.subtitle: Locked in permanently at the moment the vow is spoken

boxes.title: Age
items: A youth who valuates an elder pays the ELDER's rate
An elder who valuates a youth pays the YOUTH's rate

boxes.title: Sex
items: A man who valuates a woman pays the WOMAN's rate
A woman who valuates a man pays the MAN's rate

boxes.title: Timing
items: The rate LOCKS IN at the moment the vow is spoken — even if the subject's age bracket changes before payment

callout.label: The Gemara's analogy:
callout.text: Just as a pearl is assessed by its immediate, local market rather than a distant one, a valuation is fixed at that moment — the same principle that values a vital limb by the dignity of the whole person.

slides.title: 📅 Where Exactly Do the Age Brackets Switch Over?
slides.subtitle: A verbal analogy, and Rabbi Eliezer's stricter reading

lines.speaker: Tanna Kamma
lines.text: Day 30 counts as 'under a month'; likewise, year 5 and year 20 count as 'under' the next bracket — derived by comparing the word 'year' used for age 60 ('and upward') to the same word used for ages 5 and 20.

lines.speaker: Objection
lines.text: But that comparison could cut the WRONG way — using it to make ages 5 and 20 more LENIENT, unlike 60, which is more stringent!

lines.speaker: Resolved
lines.text: The verbal analogy applies both ways, for leniency AND stringency alike, since both mentions of 'year' are otherwise superfluous ('free') in their verses.

lines.speaker: Rabbi Eliezer dissents
lines.text: Not just one day — a FULL EXTRA MONTH is needed past each threshold, derived instead from a comparison to the census of the Levites, 'from a month old and upward.'

slides.title: 🗓️ 'A Year' Across the Torah — Calendar, or Exact Anniversary?
slides.subtitle: A baraita surveys several Torah periods, each calculated from its own starting point
rows: Counted from ITS OWN birth, not the calendar
'A sheep in ITS year' — not 'the year'
Redeeming a house in a walled city (1 year)
From the DATE OF SALE, not the calendar year
'Until the completion of the year of its sale'
An exact anniversary, allowing up to 3 harvests in under 2 years
The plural 'years of crops' implies flexible timing
An exact anniversary — may spill into a 7th calendar year
'Six years he shall serve, AND in the seventh' — not simply 'the seventh'

summary.principle: The daf closes by locating precise boundaries everywhere it can: a witness's fitness need only bracket the ends of the process, a leper's poverty is measured strictly by what he actually possesses now, a valuation locks in at the instant it is spoken, the Torah's age brackets pivot exactly where its own verses signal, and Torah-mandated 'years' run from their own starting event rather than the calendar.

flowSteps.content: 🧑‍⚖️ A witness fit at both ends of the process remains valid despite interim disqualification
💰 A leper stays 'poor' until an inheritance or rent is actually, legally his — not merely anticipated

columns.content: ⚖️ Valuation locks to the subject's age/sex at the moment of the vow, like a pearl priced in its own market
📅🗓️ Age brackets and Torah 'years' each pivot at a precisely derived point, not the calendar's own boundaries

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: halakhic status is fixed at the exact legal moment specified by the Torah's own language — never assumed early, and never left to the calendar's convenience

quiz.q: According to the baraita's principle, when is a witness who became temporarily unfit (for example, went deaf or blind) between seeing an event and testifying about it still considered valid?
o: Never — any interim disqualification permanently invalidates him
If he was fit both at the beginning (when he saw the event) and at the end (when he testifies), regardless of any interim period of disqualification
Only if he was unfit for less than one day
Only if a court explicitly reinstates him
quiz.e: The baraita's stated principle is that fitness at the beginning and end of the process suffices, even with disqualification in between.

quiz.q: Why is a leper still considered 'poor' even though his dying father is about to leave him a fortune?
o: Because inheritances are never counted toward wealth
Because he does not legally inherit the money until his father actually dies, and a majority of moribund people eventually dying does not change his status early
Because the leper renounced his inheritance
Because Jewish law forbids inheriting while a parent is alive under any circumstance
quiz.e: The Gemara clarifies the case refers to a father who is dying but has not yet died — the son has no legal claim to the money until the death actually occurs.

quiz.q: According to the new mishna, whose age and sex determine the sum owed in a valuation vow?
o: The person being valuated (the subject), not the one who takes the vow
The one who takes the vow (the vower), not the subject
Whichever party is older
The Temple treasurer decides case by case
quiz.e: The mishna states that the age-based sum and the male/female distinction both follow the person being valuated, in contrast to affordability, which follows the vower.

quiz.q: According to the mishna's ruling about the age brackets (under 5, under 20, under 60) and its accompanying verbal analogy, how is the transition point at each threshold determined?
o: By comparing the word 'year' used for the explicit 'sixty years and upward' bracket to the same word used for the 5- and 20-year brackets, applying the rule both leniently and stringently
By simple majority vote among the Sages
By counting from the person's birthday on the Jewish calendar only
There is no fixed rule; it varies case by case
quiz.e: The Gemara derives via gezeira shava that the same 'incomplete year counts as the lower bracket' rule from age 60 applies equally to ages 5 and 20, in both directions.

quiz.q: According to the baraita, how is the Torah's 'one year' period calculated for a sacrificial animal, a walled-city house redemption, and similar cases?
o: According to the fixed calendar year (Rosh Hashanah to Rosh Hashanah)
As an exact anniversary from the specific starting event (birth, sale, etc.), not according to the calendar year
According to the lunar month only
There is no consistent method; each case is unrelated
quiz.e: The baraita establishes that these Torah-stated year periods run 'from time to time' — an exact anniversary from their own starting point — rather than aligning with the calendar year.
